name: The Founding Wound: Nation-State Collapse in the Lakes Corri
description: One of the earliest documentary attempts to record firsthand testimony from survivors of the nation-state dissolution period in the Great Lakes region, capturing voices that were already aging out of memory — former municipal workers, displaced community organizers, people who remembered when Chicago and Milwaukee had mayors. Made with minimal funding and flat-screen distribution, its rough production values are now considered part of its authenticity. The director, Iosefa Nakamura-Dahl, died of illness in 2187 before the film gained its current reputation.
cultural_impact: Considered the founding document of the Meridian independent documentary tradition — virtually every underground filmmaker in M88 claims it as an influence, and bootleg copies have circulated continuously since its initial broadcast.
story_hooks: A subject in the film references a physical cache of pre-collapse municipal records hidden during the dissolution; no one has ever found it.
A corponation legal team is attempting to claim retroactive rights to the footage on the grounds that some locations filmed are now sovereign territory, which would allow them to suppress it.
Someone is making a documentary about the documentary — and discovering that Nakamura-Dahl's death may not have been from illness.
